items.extra: je / j'（元音或哑音 h 前省音）
items.zh: 我（主语：说话人自己）
items.en: I (subject: the speaker)
items.sen: I am carrying a blue bag.
items.scene: Ninon is the visibly speaking adult: her mouth is open, one hand holds a blue bag and her free hand touches her own chest. Pia faces her as the silent listener, with empty hands. Ninon's wordless speech bubble contains a tiny picture of that same bag. Emphasize the speaker performing the action, not merely a portrait. Swapping je for tu would assign the bag to empty-handed Pia; elle would require a third person outside this speaker-listener pair.
items.hook: je 指正在说话的“我”；看谁开口、谁提包。
items.style: Flat vector illustration: bold clean shapes, crisp outlines, minimal flat shading, bright friendly palette

items.extra: tu
items.zh: 你（主语：对一个熟悉的人说）
items.en: you (singular familiar subject)
items.sen: You are carrying a blue bag.
items.scene: Ninon speaks directly to Pia, looking at Pia's eyes with her mouth open and one open hand indicating Pia. Pia is the silent listener and holds a blue bag; Ninon's hands are empty. Keep the speaker, listener and bag in one clear triangle. A wordless bubble attached to Ninon contains Pia carrying the bag. Swapping tu for je would make the empty-handed speaker the carrier; elle would change the addressee into someone being discussed.
items.hook: tu 是面对一个熟悉的人说“你”；提包的是听话的人。
items.style: Watercolor storybook illustration: translucent pigment washes, visible paper grain, clean readable focal relationships

items.extra: il / elle（本条先学第三人称单数主语）
items.zh: 他／她／它（第三人称单数主语）
items.en: he / she / it (third-person singular subject)
items.sen: She is carrying a blue bag.
items.scene: Ninon speaks to Lison in the foreground; their eye contact clearly makes Lison the listener. Both have empty hands. Ninon gestures sideways toward Pia, a separate third person walking with a blue bag a few steps away. Pia is looking ahead, not participating in their conversation. A wordless bubble from Ninon shows the bag. Swapping elle for tu would identify empty-handed Lison as the carrier; je would identify empty-handed Ninon.
items.hook: elle 是被谈到的“她”，既不是说话人，也不是听话人。
items.style: Colored-pencil illustration: delicate layered pencil strokes, warm paper texture, clear expressive characters

items.extra: nous（主语、直接／间接宾语、重读和反身用法同形）
items.zh: 我们／给我们（包括说话人的一组人）
items.en: we / us / to us (a group including the speaker)
items.sen: We are carrying a large bag.
items.szh: 我们正一起提着一个大包。
items.scene: Ninon and Pia share the weight of one oversized bag, each holding one handle. Ninon speaks to Lison, who stands apart with empty hands; Ninon's free hand makes an inclusive gesture from herself to Pia. Pia looks toward their listener. The central relation is a group that visibly includes the speaking carrier. Swapping nous for vous would exclude Ninon and address a different carrying group, contradicting her active grip and Lison's empty hands.
items.hook: nous 包括说话人自己；画中开口的 Ninon 也在提包。
items.style: Gouache picture-book illustration: opaque matte brushwork, saturated color blocks, soft handmade edges

items.extra: vous（复数或礼貌单数；主语、宾语、重读和反身用法同形）
items.zh: 你们／您（复数听者或礼貌称呼）
items.en: you / to you (plural or polite singular)
items.sen: You are carrying a large bag.
items.szh: 你们正一起提着一个大包。
items.scene: Ninon stands apart, empty-handed, visibly speaking to both Lison and Pia. Lison and Pia face Ninon while each holds one handle of the same oversized bag. Ninon's open gesture spans both listeners. Keep all three faces and both carrying hands visible. Swapping vous for nous would wrongly include empty-handed Ninon; elles would mean discussing the two carriers instead of directly addressing them, so retain clear eye contact toward the speaker.
items.hook: vous 在这里是“你们”；两个提包的人都是听话人。
items.style: Layered cut-paper collage: crisp cut silhouettes, tactile paper fibers, gentle layered shadows

items.extra: ils / elles（全为阴性时用 elles）
items.zh: 他们／她们／它们（第三人称复数主语）
items.en: they (third-person plural subject)
items.sen: They are carrying a large bag.
items.szh: 她们正一起提着一个大包。
items.scene: Ninon in the foreground turns toward the viewer, mouth open as though telling the viewer something. She gestures behind her toward Lison and Pia, who jointly carry a large bag farther away. The carriers look toward their path, not at Ninon, and do not take part in the foreground conversation. Swapping elles for nous would include Ninon, who is not carrying; vous would directly address the carriers, contrary to the established speaking direction.
items.hook: elles 指谈话之外的“她们”；只有女性的一组人用 elles。
items.style: Multi-color woodblock print: carved line texture, aligned color layers, bold shapes; preserve all signature character colors

items.extra: on（动词用第三人称单数；口语可指 nous）
items.zh: 人们／咱们（泛指主语；动词用单数）
items.en: people / we (indefinite subject with a singular verb)
items.sen: Here, people wash their hands.
items.scene: Show a friendly shared wash area as a general routine, with Ninon, Pia and Lison independently washing their own hands at separate sinks, plus an empty clean sink ready for the next visitor. No one is addressing a specific listener. A small wordless bubble of two hands under running water repeats the common activity. Emphasize an unspecified reusable practice, not one named person's turn. Swapping on for tu narrows this to one addressee; the general reading of on versus a particular nous group still depends on the sentence and cannot be guaranteed by a silent image alone.
items.hook: on 可泛指“人们”；这里说一般做法，后面的动词仍用单数。
items.style: Handmade clay diorama: smooth sculpted forms, subtle fingerprints, softly lit miniature set

items.extra: moi（介词后、强调或单独回答；moi-même = 我自己）
items.zh: 我（重读：用于介词后或强调自己）
items.en: me (stressed: after a preposition or for emphasis)
items.sen: This bag belongs to me.
items.scene: Ninon visibly speaks to Lison while holding a blue bag close to her own side. She points firmly to her chest with her free hand, a warm but emphatic ownership gesture. Lison listens with empty hands. Keep the bag connected to Ninon's arm and body, not being passed toward Lison. Swapping moi for toi would assign the bag to the listener. The emphatic self-reference is visible; the requirement to use the stressed form after à comes from the sentence.
items.hook: 介词 à 后用重读形式 moi；à moi 表示“属于我”。
items.style: Pixel art illustration: coherent crisp square pixels, carefully dithered shading, readable character silhouettes and eye colors

items.extra: toi（介词后、强调或单独回答；toi-même = 你自己）
items.zh: 你（重读：用于介词后或强调对方）
items.en: you (stressed singular familiar form)
items.sen: This present is for you.
items.scene: Ninon speaks directly to Pia while offering a neatly wrapped present toward her. Pia faces Ninon and reaches to accept it; Ninon's free hand points gently toward Pia, not toward her own chest. Make the direction of giving and the listener's receiving hands the focal point. Swapping toi for moi would reverse the intended recipient to the speaker. The image makes the addressee-recipient clear; the stressed form after pour is carried by the sentence.
items.hook: pour 后用重读形式 toi；礼物给正在听话的“你”。
items.style: Retro illustrated poster aesthetic: bold vintage composition and limited shading, no typography or lettering

items.extra: lui（间接宾语：给他或她；重读阳性）；重读阴性 elle
items.zh: 给他／她（间接宾语）；他（重读）
items.en: to him / her (indirect object); him (stressed)
items.sen: Ninon gives her an apple.
items.scene: Ninon extends one apple to Pia, whose open receiving hand is the visual focal point. Lison stands slightly aside as an observing speaker, mouth open and hand indicating Pia rather than the apple. Keep the giver, the separate apple and the single recipient unmistakable. A restrained curved motion trail follows the apple toward Pia without any written marks. Swapping lui for leur requires multiple recipients; replacing the recipient with a direct-object pronoun would change which part of the giving relation is being referred to.
items.hook: lui 在这里指“给她”，不是苹果；苹果是被递出的直接宾语。
items.style: Isometric stylized 3D diorama: clear geometry, friendly adult characters, soft global illumination

items.extra: eux / elles（重读复数）
items.zh: 他们／她们（重读：用于介词后或强调）
items.en: them (stressed: after a preposition or for emphasis)
items.sen: Pia walks with them.
items.scene: Ninon and Lison walk together as an already recognizable pair; Pia joins beside them and walks in the same direction at the same pace. Show relaxed shared eye contact and an inclusive arc formed by their linked arms, keeping Pia visually distinct from the pair referred to. The narrator is outside the scene; none of the three addresses the viewer. Swapping elles for elle would refer to only one companion, while moi would introduce the speaker as a companion. The stressed form after avec is sentence-level information.
items.hook: avec 后用重读代词；elles 在这里指 Ninon 和 Lison 两个人。
items.style: Ink and light color wash: flowing ink contours with airy pigment washes, retaining each character's full signature palette

items.extra: me / m'（动词前的直接、间接宾语或反身形式）
items.zh: 我／给我／我自己（动词前宾语或反身）
items.en: me / to me / myself (object or reflexive before a verb)
items.sen: Ninon gives me an apple.
items.scene: Pia is the visibly speaking recipient, mouth open toward Lison as she receives an apple from Ninon. Ninon's hand carries the apple toward Pia's open palm; Lison is the empty-handed listener beside them. Pia lightly indicates her own chest with her other hand. The speaker's receiving hand and the giving direction must dominate. Swapping me for te would send the apple to Lison, the listener, while lui would refer to a third person instead of speaking Pia.
items.hook: me 在这里是“给我”；接苹果的人就是正在开口的 Pia。
items.style: Risograph illustration: visible grain, slightly offset ink layers, bold graphic shapes; retain signature hair, eye and dress colors

items.extra: te / t'（动词前的直接、间接宾语或反身形式）
items.zh: 你／给你／你自己（动词前单数熟称宾语或反身）
items.en: you / to you / yourself (singular familiar object or reflexive)
items.sen: Ninon gives you an apple.
items.scene: Pia speaks directly to Lison with her mouth open and her hand indicating Lison's receiving palm. Ninon passes one apple to Lison. Pia's hands remain empty, and Lison looks toward Pia while accepting Ninon's apple. Use the same simple giving triangle as a pronoun lesson, with the apple clearly travelling to the listener. Swapping te for me would make speaking Pia the recipient, contradicting the visible handoff.
items.hook: te 在这里是“给你”；苹果递给正在听话的 Lison。
items.style: Chibi cartoon: cute large heads and small rounded bodies, adult character identities and hairstyles, clean lively silhouettes

items.extra: le / la / l' / les（本条为代词；l' 是 le、la 的省音）
items.zh: 他／她／它／他们等（直接宾语：动作直接作用的对象）
items.en: him / her / it / them (direct object pronoun)
items.sen: Pia is eating this cake.
items.scene: Pia uses a fork to take a bite directly from one small cake. A discreet inset shows the same distinctive whole cake before the bite, linked visually to the cake on the plate; it is a referent reminder, not a second available cake. The main focus is the cake as the object being eaten, with fork, mouth and missing bite forming a clear path. No other recipient appears. Swapping le for lui would confuse the eaten object with an indirect recipient; the sentence establishes the direct-object grammar.
items.hook: le 代替前面的 gâteau；它直接承受“吃”这个动作。
items.style: Flat vector illustration: bold clean shapes, crisp outlines, minimal flat shading, bright friendly palette

items.extra: leur（代词不加 s；不同于 leur / leurs 限定词）
items.zh: 给他们／她们（复数间接宾语）
items.en: to them (plural indirect object)
items.sen: Ninon gives them apples.
items.scene: Ninon stands before Lison and Pia and gives an apple to each of them. Both recipients' open hands are clearly visible, each receiving one fruit; Ninon remains the only giver. The central composition branches from one giver to two separate receivers. Keep unused fruit in a small basket rather than suggesting extra recipients. Swapping leur for lui would reduce the referred-to recipients to one, leaving the simultaneous second handoff unexplained.
items.hook: leur 指“给她们”，对应多个接受者；代词 leur 不加 s。
items.style: Watercolor storybook illustration: translucent pigment washes, visible paper grain, clean readable focal relationships

items.extra: se / s'（第三人称单复数共用）；相关重读形式 soi / soi-même（主语泛指时）
items.zh: 他／她／它自己；他们自己（第三人称反身）
items.en: himself / herself / itself / themselves (third-person reflexive)
items.sen: Pia washes her hands.
items.scene: Pia alone at a low washbasin rubs her own two hands together under running water. Show both forearms continuously connected to her body and her gaze directed at her hands, so the action clearly returns to the same person who performs it. No helper or second pair of hands is present. Swapping se for lui would make someone else the recipient of the washing action; me would imply the speaker's hands rather than Pia's.
items.hook: se 让动作回到主语自己：Pia 洗的是自己的手。
items.style: Colored-pencil illustration: delicate layered pencil strokes, warm paper texture, clear expressive characters

items.extra: y（代替地点，或 à + 事物）
items.zh: 在那里／到那里；对此（代替地点或 à 引出的事物）
items.en: there / to it (replaces a place or à + a thing)
items.sen: Ninon plays there, in the park.
items.szh: Ninon 在那里玩，也就是公园里。
items.scene: A small opening vignette establishes a park with a distinctive curved bench and one broad tree. In the large main scene, Ninon plays with a ball inside that very park; repeat the bench and tree clearly so the place is recognized. Use a soft visual link between the established place and her current location, without letters, map labels or signs. The focus is returning to an already identified place. Swapping y for en would refer to a different relation, such as origin or a quantity, not her location inside the park.
items.hook: y 代替前面已经提到的地点 au parc，避免重复说地点。
items.style: Gouache picture-book illustration: opaque matte brushwork, saturated color blocks, soft handmade edges

items.extra: en（代替 de + 事物、来源或不定数量）
items.zh: 其中一些／从那里／关于它（代替 de 短语或数量对象）
items.en: some / of it / from there (replaces de-phrases or a quantity referent)
items.sen: Pia takes two of the apples.
items.szh: 这些苹果，Pia 从中拿了两个。
items.scene: Show an open basket with several apples and Pia lifting exactly two apples from it, one in each hand. Other apples remain clearly visible in the basket. Her eyes follow the selected fruit and the short lifting path from the source basket. Do not print any numbers. The central relation is a subset taken from a previously visible quantity, not movement to a place. Swapping en for a whole-object pronoun would obscure the explicit part-from-a-set relation; the number is shown by the two held apples.
items.hook: en 接回前面的 pommes；deux 保留数量，意思是“其中两个”。
items.style: Layered cut-paper collage: crisp cut silhouettes, tactile paper fibers, gentle layered shadows

items.extra: quelqu'un / quelqu'une（少见）/ quelques-uns / quelques-unes（其中一些）
items.zh: 某个人；其中一些人或物（身份未具体说明）
items.en: someone; some of them (identity unspecified)
items.sen: Someone is knocking at our door.
items.scene: Lison is inside a welcoming home, listening at a closed door with curious raised eyebrows. Through the frosted pane, only an unidentified adult visitor's indistinct silhouette and raised knocking hand are visible; the face and identity cannot be recognized. Small motion arcs at the knuckles show knocking without any written sound. Focus on the existence of a person whose identity is unknown. Swapping quelqu'un for personne would remove the visible knocker; quelque chose would replace the human visitor with a thing.
items.hook: quelqu'un 是“有人”，身份还不知道；不是某个物品。
items.style: Multi-color woodblock print: carved line texture, aligned color layers, bold shapes; preserve all signature character colors

items.extra: quelque chose；quelque chose de + 形容词
items.zh: 某个东西／某件事（非人，尚未具体说明）
items.en: something (an unspecified thing)
items.fr: Pia cache [quelque chose] dans sa main.
items.sen: Pia hides something in her hand.
items.szh: Pia 把某个东西藏在手里。
items.scene: Pia holds one cupped hand closed around a small tangible object. A tiny rounded edge and the bulge of her fingers make its presence clear, while hiding its identity. Lison leans toward the hand with a curious expression. The focal point is an unspecified thing concealed inside the hand, never a tiny person or an empty fist. Swapping quelque chose for rien would require an empty hand; quelqu'un would wrongly suggest a hidden person.
items.hook: quelque chose 指身份未说明的东西；手里确实有物品，但看不清是什么。
items.style: Handmade clay diorama: smooth sculpted forms, subtle fingerprints, softly lit miniature set

items.extra: ne ... personne / personne ne ...（本条不是名词 une personne）
items.zh: 没有人（否定代词）
items.en: nobody / no one (negative pronoun)
items.sen: Lison sees nobody outside.
items.szh: Lison 在外面没有看见任何人。
items.scene: Lison stands indoors and looks through a wide open window onto an entirely empty courtyard. The courtyard contains clearly visible flowers, a bench and a fountain, but no people, human silhouettes or portraits. Keep Lison on the indoor side of the window frame so she does not count as someone outside. Her searching gaze sweeps the vacant path. Swapping personne for quelqu'un would require a person outdoors; rien would be false because she can plainly see the courtyard's objects.
items.hook: personne 否定的是“人”；窗外有景物，但一个人也没有。
items.style: Pixel art illustration: coherent crisp square pixels, carefully dithered shading, readable character silhouettes and eye colors

items.extra: ne ... rien / rien ne ...
items.zh: 什么也没有（否定事物）
items.en: nothing (no thing at all)
items.sen: Pia finds nothing inside.
items.szh: Pia 在里面什么也没找到。
items.scene: Pia tilts a wide open box toward the viewer so its entire clean, empty interior is visible. Her other hand lifts the loose lid, and she peers all the way to the bare bottom. Ninon stands nearby in plain sight, making the absence specifically about things inside the box, not about people in the room. No crumbs, tissue, false bottom or hidden object. Swapping rien for quelque chose would require a visible item in the box.
items.hook: rien 是“什么东西也没有”；强调盒子里面完全空着。
items.style: Retro illustrated poster aesthetic: bold vintage composition and limited shading, no typography or lettering

items.extra: chacun / chacune；chacun de ...
items.zh: 每个人／每一个（单独代替名词，逐一看待）
items.en: each one (a pronoun considering individuals separately)
items.sen: Each of them holds a small apple.
items.szh: 她们每人都拿着一个小苹果。
items.scene: Ninon, Lison and Pia stand in three gently separated positions, each holding exactly one small apple. Make all three individual hand-and-apple pairs equally prominent, with no shared basket or unserved person. The composition should invite checking the members one by one. Swapping chacune for quelqu'un would no longer communicate the one-per-person distribution. A universal group statement with toutes can also be true of this scene; the image supports individual distribution rather than uniquely encoding the grammar.
items.hook: chacune 是“每个人”，逐个检查：Ninon、Lison、Pia 一人一个。
items.style: Isometric stylized 3D diorama: clear geometry, friendly adult characters, soft global illumination

items.extra: tout（全部事情）/ tous / toutes（所有已提及的人或物）
items.zh: 一切／所有人或物（代词，单独使用）
items.en: everything / everyone / all of them (stand-alone pronoun)
items.sen: Pia puts everything in her box.
items.szh: Pia 把所有东西都放进自己的盒子里。
items.scene: Use a clear before-and-after diptych. On the left, Pia has an open empty box beside exactly a ball, a plain book and a toy duck on a bare table. On the right, all three recognizable objects are inside the box and the tabletop is completely clear. Repeat Pia and the same box faithfully across the two panels. The defining relation is complete inclusion with nothing left out. Swapping tout for rien would leave the box empty; a partial-quantity expression would leave at least one object outside.
items.hook: tout 强调整体一个不漏；桌上的三样东西全部进了盒子。
items.style: Ink and light color wash: flowing ink contours with airy pigment washes, retaining each character's full signature palette

items.extra: ce / c'；c'est / ce sont（代词作主语，后接 être）
items.zh: 这／那（用于 c'est、ce sont，引出身份或事物）
items.en: this/that (neutral subject in c'est/ce sont, identifying someone or something)
items.sen: This is Ninon with her blue bag.
items.szh: 这是 Ninon，带着她的蓝色包。
items.scene: Lison visibly introduces Ninon to Pia: Lison's mouth is open, her open palm presents Ninon as a whole person, and Pia turns to meet Ninon. Ninon stands clearly apart holding a blue bag and smiles in greeting. A wordless portrait bubble attached to Lison repeats Ninon's face, making identification the focus rather than ownership or the bag's position. Changing the identified person would change the portrait and gesture. The identifying construction c'est itself remains sentence-level grammar, not something a silent image can uniquely spell.
items.hook: c' 是 ce 在 est 前的省音；c'est 常用来介绍“这是谁／是什么”。
items.style: Risograph illustration: visible grain, slightly offset ink layers, bold graphic shapes; retain signature hair, eye and dress colors

items.extra: ça / cela（较正式）；不按指代物的性数变化
items.zh: 这件事／那个东西（中性指代，可作主语或宾语）
items.en: this / that thing or situation (neutral demonstrative)
items.sen: Pia shows that to Ninon.
items.szh: Pia 把那个东西指给 Ninon 看。
items.scene: Pia speaks to Ninon while pointing at an unusual smooth pebble shaped like a little duck on a table. Both characters' gaze converges on that one object; a small wordless bubble from Pia contains its silhouette. The pebble has no writing or face. Emphasize the act of indicating a thing without naming its noun. Replacing ça with a person-reference would not match the indicated object; the neutral demonstrative versus a noun-specific celui form still depends on the sentence context.
items.hook: ça 可以指“那个东西”，不用先说出它的名词；不是指人物。
items.style: Chibi cartoon: cute large heads and small rounded bodies, adult character identities and hairstyles, clean lively silhouettes

items.extra: celui-ci / celle-ci / ceux-ci / celles-ci
items.zh: 这个／这些（较近者，代替已知名词）
items.en: this one / these ones (the nearer referent)
items.sen: I am taking this one, near me.
items.scene: Ninon speaks while choosing between two equally attractive plain books on a long table. One book is immediately beside her hand; the other is far away at the opposite end. Ninon takes the near book, with her hand, gaze and body all directing attention to it; the far book remains untouched. Pia listens from the side. Keep both books alike so color or quality does not explain the choice. Swapping celui-ci for celui-là would select the distant book instead.
items.hook: -ci 指较近的这个；两本书中，手边这本被选中。
items.style: Flat vector illustration: bold clean shapes, crisp outlines, minimal flat shading, bright friendly palette

items.extra: celui-là / celle-là / ceux-là / celles-là
items.zh: 那个／那些（较远者，代替已知名词）
items.en: that one / those ones (the farther referent)
items.sen: I am taking that one, far from me.
items.szh: 我拿离我较远的那一个。
items.scene: Ninon speaks while choosing between two equally attractive plain books on a long table. She points distinctly across the table toward the distant book and reaches past the near book without touching it. Pia follows Ninon's pointing line from the side. Keep the books alike and both visible, with enough empty table between them to make the distance difference obvious. Swapping celui-là for celui-ci would select the untouched book beside Ninon instead.
items.hook: -là 在这句指较远的那个；不要选手边的近处书。
items.style: Watercolor storybook illustration: translucent pigment washes, visible paper grain, clean readable focal relationships

items.extra: qui（疑问：谁；关系：主语，或介词后指人）
items.zh: 谁；……的（关系从句主语，或介词后指人）
items.en: who; who / which / that (relative subject, or a person after a preposition)
items.sen: Here is Lison, who is pushing Pia.
items.szh: 这是正在推 Pia 的 Lison。
items.scene: Lison stands behind a small sturdy rolling chair and gently pushes Pia, who sits safely with feet on its footrest. Lison's hands grip the backrest, her stance shows the forward effort, and Pia's relaxed hands rest on her lap. Use a gentle motion trail under the wheels. The person introduced, Lison, is unmistakably the agent of the pushing action. Swapping qui for que in the same sentence reverses the roles and would require Pia to push Lison instead.
items.hook: qui 在关系从句里做主语：是 Lison 推 Pia。
items.style: Colored-pencil illustration: delicate layered pencil strokes, warm paper texture, clear expressive characters

items.extra: que / qu'（疑问：什么；关系：直接宾语）
items.zh: 什么；……的（关系从句的直接宾语）

items.extra: quand / lorsque / lorsqu'（lorsque 较书面，同义合并）
items.zh: 当……的时候（某事发生的时间）
items.en: when (the time at which something happens)
items.fr: [Quand] le soleil se lève, Ninon se réveille.
items.sen: When the sun rises, Ninon wakes up.
items.scene: Two aligned panels depict the same dawn moment. On the left the sun is just crossing the horizon; on the right the first matching golden rays reach Ninon's room as she opens her eyes and sits up. A continuous band of dawn light visually links the two panels. Her blue dress and cream headband remain identifiable. Emphasize the onset of sunrise coinciding with waking, not a long elapsed interval or an imagined condition. Keep a friendly, relaxed mood. No written text, letters, numerals, logos or watermarks.
items.hook: quand 给动作标出发生的时间：太阳升起的时候，人也醒来。
items.style: Gouache picture-book illustration: opaque matte brushwork, saturated color blocks, soft handmade edges

items.extra: que / qu'；dire que / penser que
items.zh: 引出所说、所想的内容（宾语从句）
items.en: that (introducing what is said or thought)
items.fr: Lison dit [que] Pia aime les chats.
items.sen: Lison says that Pia likes cats.
items.scene: Lison is clearly speaking to Ninon, with an open speaking mouth and a speech bubble whose tail points only to Lison. Inside that bubble, show a miniature but recognizable Pia happily cuddling a cat. The complete little scene inside the bubble represents the CONTENT of Lison's statement. Do not place a written sentence or punctuation in the bubble, and do not make the cat a physical object being passed between the speakers. Keep a friendly, relaxed mood. No written text, letters, numerals, logos or watermarks.
items.hook: 连词 que 引出“说的内容”：气泡里整件事是 Lison 说的话。
items.style: Layered cut-paper collage: crisp cut silhouettes, tactile paper fibers, gentle layered shadows

items.extra: comme；比较“像……一样”，句首也可表原因“由于”
items.zh: 像……一样；由于（比较，或置于句首的原因）
items.en: as / like; since (comparison, or a cause placed first)
items.sen: Pia dances as Ninon does.
items.scene: A two-panel comparison: Ninon demonstrates a simple adult dance pose in the left panel, with one arm curved above her head and the other extended sideways; Pia watches her and copies the exact same arm, hand and foot positions in the right panel. Preserve their different character designs. The visual match is in HOW they dance, supported by Pia's attentive gaze toward the demonstration, not merely by both being on a dance floor. Keep a friendly, relaxed mood. No written text, letters, numerals, logos or watermarks.
items.hook: comme 在这里比较做法：Pia照着Ninon的姿势跳。
items.style: Multi-color woodblock print: carved line texture, aligned color layers, bold shapes; preserve all signature character colors

items.extra: car（通常接在前一个判断之后）
items.zh: 因为；要知道（补充理由，解释前面的判断）
items.en: for / because (justifying a preceding statement)
items.fr: Pia est là, [car] sa lumière est allumée.
items.sen: Pia is there, for her light is on.
items.szh: Pia在那里，因为她房间的灯亮着。
items.scene: An evidence-and-inference diptych at dusk: Ninon stands outside Pia's home and notices a warm lamp glowing behind a frosted window. In the second panel Ninon thoughtfully indicates that same lit window while a small thought bubble shows recognizable Pia inside at her desk. Pia's actual presence is not directly revealed through the frosted glass. The lamp is evidence supporting Ninon's judgment that Pia is home; it does not physically cause Pia to be there. Keep a friendly, relaxed mood. No written text, letters, numerals, logos or watermarks.
items.hook: car 补充判断的理由：灯亮着是“Pia在家”的线索，不是让她在家的原因。
items.style: Handmade clay diorama: smooth sculpted forms, subtle fingerprints, softly lit miniature set

items.extra: puisque / puisqu'
items.zh: 既然（以显而易见或双方已知的原因作依据）
items.en: since / seeing that (an evident or shared reason)
items.fr: [Puisque] tu es là, nous mangeons ensemble.
items.sen: Since you are here, we are eating together.
items.szh: 既然你在这里，我们就一起吃饭。
items.scene: A welcoming diptych: the first panel shows Ninon and Pia already facing each other inside the doorway, making mutual eye contact and greeting each other, so Pia's presence is an obvious fact known to both. The second shows Ninon, clearly the speaker, including Pia with an open-arm invitation as they sit at a table set for two and actively eat their meal together, both holding food or utensils over their plates. Keep the already-shared fact of being there as the basis for the meal; no uncertain weather bubble, investigation or surprise discovery. Keep a friendly, relaxed mood. No written text, letters, numerals, logos or watermarks.
items.hook: puisque 从双方已经知道的事实出发：你已经在这里，那我们一起吃。
items.style: Pixel art illustration: coherent crisp square pixels, carefully dithered shading, readable character silhouettes and eye colors

items.extra: pendant que / pendant qu'
items.zh: 在……的同时（两项活动同时进行）
items.en: while (two activities taking place at the same time)
items.sen: Ninon reads while Pia draws.
items.scene: A split view of one continuous room shows Ninon reading an open picture book in the left half and Pia drawing a simple cat in the right half. The same uninterrupted sunlight, shared table edge and window view run through both halves, making it unmistakable that the two ongoing activities happen at the same time. Neither character has finished or caused the other's activity. The book and drawing contain pictures only, never letters. Keep a friendly, relaxed mood. No written text, letters, numerals, logos or watermarks.
items.hook: pendant que 强调两个动作同时进行：一个读，一个画。
items.style: Retro illustrated poster aesthetic: bold vintage composition and limited shading, no typography or lettering

items.extra: alors que / alors qu'（也可表示同时）
items.zh: 而；却（对照两个不同的事实）
items.en: whereas (contrasting two different facts)
items.fr: Ninon a chaud, [alors que] Pia a froid.
items.sen: Ninon feels hot, whereas Pia feels cold.
items.scene: Two equal contrasting panels: Ninon sits in a bright sunny garden spot, fanning herself with an open hand and showing a few warm-weather perspiration drops; Pia sits in the deep cool shade nearby, hugging her arms and wrapping a light blanket over her white dress. Keep them in the same garden and time of day. Their opposite bodily reactions, hot versus cold, are the focus; do not suggest that one causes the other's feeling. Keep a friendly, relaxed mood. No written text, letters, numerals, logos or watermarks.
items.hook: alors que 在这里把相反的事实放在一起：这边热，那边冷。
items.style: Isometric stylized 3D diorama: clear geometry, friendly adult characters, soft global illumination

items.extra: même si / même s'（仅在 il / ils 前省音）
items.zh: 即使；尽管（条件不改变结果）
items.en: even if / even though (a condition that does not change the result)
items.sen: Pia goes out even if it rains.
items.scene: Show Pia at her doorway with a determined friendly expression. Two clearly hypothetical small scenes float within one imagination bubble: in one she walks outside in sunshine; in the other she walks outside in rain with an umbrella. Her route out of the door and forward walking pose are the same in both. The weather changes but the decision to go out does not. Keep both possible situations visibly imagined, with no text or weather labels. Keep a friendly, relaxed mood. No written text, letters, numerals, logos or watermarks.
items.hook: même si 表示这个条件也不改变结果；même s'il 中 si 省音。无论晴雨，她都出门。
items.style: Ink and light color wash: flowing ink contours with airy pigment washes, retaining each character's full signature palette

items.extra: depuis que / depuis qu'
items.zh: 自从……以来（用一个事件说明开始时间）
items.en: since (starting from the event in a clause)
items.fr: Pia sourit [depuis que] Ninon est arrivée.
items.sen: Pia has been smiling since Ninon arrived.
items.scene: A continuous three-moment strip shows the starting event and an ongoing state: on the left Ninon arrives at Pia's doorway and Pia's smile begins; in the middle they sit together while Pia is still smiling; on the right time has gently advanced through the shifted natural sunlight and Pia continues the same smile. Keep Ninon's arrival the clearly visible starting point, and maintain Pia's happy expression throughout the later moments. No written timeline, clocks with numerals or unrelated events. Keep a friendly, relaxed mood. No written text, letters, numerals, logos or watermarks.
items.hook: depuis que 用事件作起点：Ninon到来之后，Pia的笑容一直持续到现在。
items.style: Risograph illustration: visible grain, slightly offset ink layers, bold graphic shapes; retain signature hair, eye and dress colors

items.extra: le / la / l' / les；à + le → au，à + les → aux；de + le → du，de + les → des
items.zh: 这／那（些）已知的人或物（定冠词）
items.en: the (a person or thing already identified; definite article)
items.sen: Pia takes Ninon's book.
items.scene: A recognition diptych. In a small introductory panel Ninon shows Pia one distinctive plain blue book with a bent cream-coloured corner. In the larger panel Pia recognizes and picks that exact same blue book from several other plain books, while looking back toward Ninon. Repeat the same bent corner so it is already identified, not an arbitrary new book. The earlier shared identification and later recognition are the central visual relationship. Keep a friendly, relaxed mood. No written text, letters, numerals, logos or watermarks.
items.hook: le 指已经知道是哪一本；先认过，再从其他书里找到同一本。
items.style: Chibi cartoon: cute large heads and small rounded bodies, adult character identities and hairstyles, clean lively silhouettes

items.extra: un / une（单数）；复数 des 单列
items.zh: 一个未特指的人或物（单数不定冠词）
items.en: a/an (one unspecified person or thing; singular indefinite article)
items.sen: Pia takes a book.
items.scene: Pia stands before a row of many equally plain books and playfully closes her eyes as she reaches out and picks exactly one arbitrary book. No book has been singled out beforehand, labelled, pointed to by anyone else or shown in an earlier panel. Leave the remaining books in the row and emphasize her random, nonselective reach. This is one unspecified member of a set, not the retrieval of a known special book. Keep a friendly, relaxed mood. No written text, letters, numerals, logos or watermarks.
items.hook: un 在这里是未指定的“一本”：闭眼随手拿，哪一本都可以。
items.style: Flat vector illustration: bold clean shapes, crisp outlines, minimal flat shading, bright friendly palette

items.extra: des（复数）；单数 un / une 单列；不是 de + les 的缩合用法
items.zh: 一些可数的人或物（复数不定冠词）
items.en: some (unspecified countable people or things; plural indefinite article)
items.sen: Lison buys some apples at the market.
items.scene: At an unlabelled market stall, Lison places several separate whole apples into her shopping basket from a much larger pile. Make the individual apples unmistakably countable and show more than one, while avoiding any number labels or emphasis on an exact count. The selected apples are ordinary unspecified members of the pile, not one named apple, all the apples, or an uncountable liquid. A few small plain, unmarked coins on the counter beside her free hand establish a purchase; the coins carry no lettering, logos or numerical denominations. Keep a friendly, relaxed mood. No written text, letters, numerals, logos or watermarks.
items.hook: des 是可数名词前的复数不定冠词：不止一个，但没有说是哪几个。
items.style: Watercolor storybook illustration: translucent pigment washes, visible paper grain, clean readable focal relationships

items.extra: du / de la / de l'（本条学习不可数名词前的部分冠词）
items.zh: 一些不可数的东西（部分冠词，如水、面包）
items.en: some/an amount of (an uncountable substance; partitive article)
items.fr: Ninon verse [du] lait dans son bol.
items.sen: Ninon pours some milk into her bowl.
items.szh: Ninon往自己的碗里倒了一些牛奶。
items.scene: Close focus on Ninon pouring a smooth continuous stream of milk from an unlabelled jug into a bowl. A modest amount fills the bottom of the bowl while milk clearly remains in the jug. The milk is shown as an uncountable substance and portion, not as a set of countable bottles or a whole container being handed over. Preserve Ninon's visible blue dress, red waves and cream headband. Keep a friendly, relaxed mood. No written text, letters, numerals, logos or watermarks.
items.hook: du 在这里表示不可数食物的一部分：倒一些牛奶，而不是数几个瓶子。
items.style: Colored-pencil illustration: delicate layered pencil strokes, warm paper texture, clear expressive characters

items.extra: ce / cet（阳性单数，紧接元音或哑音 h 开头的词时）/ cette / ces；可加 -ci / -là 区分近远
items.zh: 这／那个，这／那些（指着名词所指的人或物）
items.en: this/that; these/those (pointing out a person or thing before a noun)
items.sen: Pia wants this cake beside her.
items.szh: Pia想要她身边的这个蛋糕。
items.scene: Pia stands close to a small cake on the near edge of a display table and points directly at it with one clear extended finger, her fingertip almost touching its plate. Other cakes sit farther away and receive no gesture. Her eyes and a speech bubble containing only a miniature picture of that selected cake point to the same near cake. Make the demonstrative act of singling out THIS cake central, not a random grab. Keep a friendly, relaxed mood. No written text, letters, numerals, logos or watermarks.
items.hook: ce 直接指出某个东西；这里由手指和视线共同锁定近处这个蛋糕。
items.style: Gouache picture-book illustration: opaque matte brushwork, saturated color blocks, soft handmade edges

items.extra: mon / ma / mes；阴性单数 ma 在紧接元音或哑音 h 开头的词前改用 mon；复数仍用 mes
items.zh: 我的（名词前，物主是说话人自己）
items.en: my (before a noun; belonging to the speaker)
items.sen: I am carrying my red bag.
items.szh: 我正拿着我自己的红色包。
items.scene: Lison is the clearly visible speaker, addressing Ninon with an open speaking mouth. Lison carries her own plain red bag with one hand and touches her own chest with the other. A small speech bubble with its tail anchored to Lison contains a miniature image of Lison herself holding the same red bag. Ninon listens without touching the bag. Ownership belongs to the speaker herself, established by the self-point and speaker-linked image, not by colour alone. Keep a friendly, relaxed mood. No written text, letters, numerals, logos or watermarks.
items.hook: mon 是说话人的“我的”；看谁在说话、谁指着自己，不只看包的颜色。
items.style: Layered cut-paper collage: crisp cut silhouettes, tactile paper fibers, gentle layered shadows

items.extra: ton / ta / tes；阴性单数 ta 在紧接元音或哑音 h 开头的词前改用 ton；复数仍用 tes
items.zh: 你的（名词前，物主是一个熟悉的听话人）
items.en: your (before a noun; belonging to one familiar addressee)
items.sen: Pia, I am carrying your white bag.
items.szh: Pia，我正替你拿着你的白色包。
items.scene: A small opening panel establishes Pia owning a plain white bag by showing her taking it from her own coat hook and handing it to Ninon. In the main panel Ninon carries that bag and speaks directly to Pia with clear eye contact and an open mouth; a nonverbal speech bubble anchored to Ninon contains a miniature Pia holding the bag. Pia is the addressed listener and owner, while Ninon merely carries it. The item in the speaker's hand therefore belongs to YOU, not to the speaker. Keep a friendly, relaxed mood. No written text, letters, numerals, logos or watermarks.
items.hook: ton 指听话人的“你的”；Ninon拿着包，但所有者是她正对着说话的Pia。
items.style: Multi-color woodblock print: carved line texture, aligned color layers, bold shapes; preserve all signature character colors

items.extra: son / sa / ses；按所修饰名词的性数配合；阴性单数 sa 在紧接元音或哑音 h 开头的词前改用 son；复数仍用 ses
items.zh: 他／她的（名词前，物主是谈到的一个人）
items.en: his/her (before a noun; belonging to one person being discussed)
items.sen: Pia arrives with her white bag.
items.szh: Pia带着她自己的白色包来了。
items.scene: Pia approaches from a short distance carrying her familiar plain white bag. In the foreground Lison speaks to Ninon and gestures toward Pia and her bag; Ninon looks where Lison points. A small speech bubble anchored to Lison shows the approaching Pia holding the bag. Pia is neither the current speaker nor the listener: she is the third person they are talking about, and the bag stays with her. Keep a friendly, relaxed mood. No written text, letters, numerals, logos or watermarks.
items.hook: son 指谈到的那个人的东西；这里说话人与听话人之外，包属于Pia。
items.style: Handmade clay diorama: smooth sculpted forms, subtle fingerprints, softly lit miniature set

items.extra: notre / nos
items.zh: 我们的（名词前，物主包括说话人在内的一群人）
items.en: our (before a noun; belonging to a group including the speaker)
items.sen: Here is our little house.
items.scene: Ninon and Pia stand together just inside the gate of their little home, jointly holding the same house key between them. Ninon is visibly speaking to Lison, who stands outside as a visitor. Ninon's free arm includes both herself and Pia before opening toward their house; a speech bubble anchored to Ninon shows both owners together beside the house. The ownership group includes the speaker, so the focal idea is OUR shared home. Keep a friendly, relaxed mood. No written text, letters, numerals, logos or watermarks.
items.hook: notre 的所有者包括说话人：Ninon把自己和Pia一起圈进“我们”。
items.style: Pixel art illustration: coherent crisp square pixels, carefully dithered shading, readable character silhouettes and eye colors

items.extra: votre / vos
items.zh: 你们的／您的（名词前，复数或敬称物主）
items.en: your (before a noun; plural addressees or one formal addressee)
items.sen: Ninon, Pia, here is your house.
items.scene: Lison stands outside a small home's gate as a visiting speaker and addresses both Ninon and Pia, who stand together inside holding the home's key jointly. Lison gestures toward the house and then toward both listeners, keeping herself outside the ownership group. A speech bubble attached to Lison shows Ninon and Pia beside their home. The two addressed listeners own the house; the speaker does not. Keep a friendly, relaxed mood. No written text, letters, numerals, logos or watermarks.
items.hook: votre 在这里是“你们的”：说话人Lison面对两个听者，但自己不属于物主群体。
items.style: Retro illustrated poster aesthetic: bold vintage composition and limited shading, no typography or lettering

items.extra: leur / leurs；按被拥有的东西的单复数配合
items.zh: 他们／她们的（名词前，物主是不含说话人的多人）
items.en: their (before a noun; belonging to other people)
items.sen: Ninon and Pia open their door.
items.scene: Ninon and Pia jointly unlock and open their own house door, both clearly associated with the house key and the welcoming interior. Lison remains in the foreground as an outside observer, speaking toward the viewer with an open mouth and indicating the two owners at the door. A nonverbal speech bubble attached to Lison depicts Ninon and Pia beside that same door. The house belongs to the two people being discussed, excluding the speaker and addressee. Keep a friendly, relaxed mood. No written text, letters, numerals, logos or watermarks.
items.hook: leur 在名词前表示“她们的”；门属于谈到的Ninon和Pia这两个人。
items.style: Isometric stylized 3D diorama: clear geometry, friendly adult characters, soft global illumination

items.extra: quel / quelle / quels / quelles（后接名词）
items.zh: 哪一个／哪些（名词前，询问选择或身份）
items.en: which/what (before a noun; asking for a choice or identity)
items.sen: Which cake do you want for your birthday?
items.szh: 你生日想要哪一个蛋糕？
items.scene: Ninon addresses Pia beside three visibly different unlabelled birthday cakes. Ninon opens one palm toward the whole set with an inquisitive raised eyebrow; Pia looks between the cakes without pointing to or taking any one yet. A speech bubble anchored to Ninon contains miniature pictures of all the alternatives, with no question mark or text. Emphasize the still-open question of WHICH cake, not a decision already made or a random choice. Keep a friendly, relaxed mood. No written text, letters, numerals, logos or watermarks.
items.hook: quel 后接名词提出选择问题；尚未指中任何一个，与 ce 的已确定指示不同。
items.style: Ink and light color wash: flowing ink contours with airy pigment washes, retaining each character's full signature palette

items.extra: chaque + 单数名词
items.zh: 每一个（后接单数名词，逐个看待）
items.en: each/every (before a singular noun; considering members one by one)
items.fr: Ninon donne une tasse à [chaque] amie.
items.sen: Ninon gives a cup to each friend.
items.scene: A two-panel one-by-one distribution: Ninon first hands a single cup to Pia, then hands a single cup to Lison. In the second panel Pia remains visible holding her own cup, and Lison receives hers, so both friends have been individually served and nobody is skipped. Emphasize one recipient and one cup at each step, not a pile handed over to the group collectively. Keep a friendly, relaxed mood. No written text, letters, numerals, logos or watermarks.
items.hook: chaque 强调逐一：先给这一位，再给下一位，每一位都照顾到。
items.style: Risograph illustration: visible grain, slightly offset ink layers, bold graphic shapes; retain signature hair, eye and dress colors

items.extra: tout / toute / tous / toutes；tout le / toute la / tous les / toutes les
items.zh: 整个／全部的（名词前，涵盖整体或所有成员）
items.en: the whole/all (before a noun; covering the entire thing or group)
items.sen: Pia takes all the biscuits.
items.scene: Show one clearly bounded serving tray containing a group of biscuits in a small before panel. In the larger result panel Pia transfers the entire group into her basket, leaving the same tray completely empty; Ninon watches with an amused friendly expression. No biscuit remains behind or off to the side. The entire known group moves together, making total coverage the focus rather than a few selected biscuits. Keep a friendly, relaxed mood. No written text, letters, numerals, logos or watermarks.
items.hook: tous 把已知的一整组全部包括：盘子空了，一块也没剩下。
items.style: Chibi cartoon: cute large heads and small rounded bodies, adult character identities and hairstyles, clean lively silhouettes

items.extra: quelques + 复数名词（本条学“少量几个”；单数 quelque 表“某个”较偏书面）
items.zh: 少量几个（名词前，数量不多但不精确）
items.en: a few (before a plural noun; a small unspecified number)
items.fr: Il reste [quelques] biscuits dans la grande boîte.
items.sen: A few biscuits remain in the large box.
items.szh: 大盒子里只剩下少量几块饼干。
items.scene: Ninon opens a very large biscuit box and finds just a small scattered handful of biscuits amid a broad empty interior and many empty dividers. Emphasize how little remains relative to the box's capacity, with a gentle slightly surprised expression. Use no numerals, counting fingers, threshold labels or claim that a particular count defines the word. This illustrates a small unspecified quantity, not zero and not the entire original supply. Keep a friendly, relaxed mood. No written text, letters, numerals, logos or watermarks.
items.hook: quelques 强调数量不多，不规定几块以上或以下；留意大盒子里只剩少量。
items.style: Flat vector illustration: bold clean shapes, crisp outlines, minimal flat shading, bright friendly palette

items.extra: plusieurs + 复数名词（阴阳性同形）
items.zh: 好几个／多个（名词前，不限定为少量）
items.en: several/multiple (before a plural noun; more than one, with no fixed count)
items.fr: Ninon porte [plusieurs] livres dans ses bras.
items.sen: Ninon is carrying several books in her arms.
items.scene: Ninon carries a clearly multi-volume stack of distinct plain books in both arms, with separate spines and edges readily visible. Make the multiplicity central: several separate volumes instead of one, with no written numbers, no exact-count gesture and no artificial boundary separating this from a few. Do not add an almost-empty container, since the focus is multiple items rather than scarcity relative to capacity. Keep a friendly, relaxed mood. No written text, letters, numerals, logos or watermarks.
items.hook: plusieurs 强调不止一个、好几个；它与 quelques 的数量范围可以重叠，不能靠固定数字硬分。
items.style: Watercolor storybook illustration: translucent pigment washes, visible paper grain, clean readable focal relationships

items.extra: aucun / aucune；ne ... aucun(e) + 通常为单数的名词
items.zh: 一个……也没有（名词前，数量为零）
items.en: no/not a single (before a noun; zero instances)
items.sen: Pia cannot find a single biscuit.
items.scene: Pia searches an open biscuit box whose whole interior is clearly visible and completely empty. She tips the box gently toward the viewer and holds her other empty palm beneath it; nothing falls out. Show no biscuit anywhere in the composition, including bubbles or decorative backgrounds. Her mildly disappointed but friendly expression reinforces zero items, not merely a small remaining quantity. Keep a friendly, relaxed mood. No written text, letters, numerals, logos or watermarks.
items.hook: aucun 是否定数量为零：盒内没有，手中也没有，一块都找不到。
items.style: Colored-pencil illustration: delicate layered pencil strokes, warm paper texture, clear expressive characters

items.extra: autre / autres；un autre / une autre / d'autres / les autres + 名词
items.zh: 另一个／别的（名词前，区别于刚才那个或那些）
items.en: another/other (before a noun; distinct from the one(s) already mentioned)
items.sen: Pia chooses another hat.

items.extra: même / mêmes；le même / la même / les mêmes + 名词
items.zh: 同一个／相同的（名词前，强调身份或样式一致）
items.en: the same (before a noun; identical in identity or kind)
items.fr: Ninon et Pia lisent le [même] livre.
items.sen: Ninon and Pia read the same book.
items.scene: Ninon and Pia sit close enough to share exactly ONE physical open book between them. Each holds one edge of the same volume, and both gazes converge on the same spread, which contains only an unlettered picture. No second book or duplicate copy appears. The two readers share a single identical referent, making sameness central rather than similar-looking separate possessions. Keep a friendly, relaxed mood. No written text, letters, numerals, logos or watermarks.
items.hook: même 强调同一个：两人的手和目光都落在唯一的那本书上。

items.extra: certain / certaine / certains / certaines；un certain / une certaine；certains / certaines + 复数名词
items.zh: 某个／某些（名词前，指特定但未明说的人或物）
items.en: a certain/some particular (before a noun; a specific but unnamed person, thing or subset)
items.fr: [Certaines] bananes sont jaunes, les autres sont vertes.
items.sen: Some of the bananas are yellow; the others are green.
items.szh: 其中一些香蕉是黄色的，其他的还是绿色的。
items.scene: Ninon examines one clearly bounded mixed bunch of bananas on a table: a specific subset is ripe yellow while the remaining bananas are visibly green. She gently separates the yellow subset with one hand while leaving the green remainder in clear view. Emphasize a particular part of the known group, distinguished by its yellow colour, not the whole bunch and not an exact number. Do not remove or hide the contrasting remainder. Keep a friendly, relaxed mood. No written text, letters, numerals, logos or watermarks.
